tutorial.title: Handling Multiple Exception Types
tutorial.descriptionContent: Handle anticipated Python exceptions with separate, specific responses.
tutorial.shortDescriptionContent: Python learners who can catch and raise built-in exceptions

lessons.title: Sample
lessons.interactiveContent:
Sometimes one generic exception handler just isn't enough. It catches almost anything that goes wrong in the try block.

This is usually too broad because it can hide unexpected problems.

Make sure to pick except.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Sometimes one generic exception handler just isn't enough. It catches almost anything that goes wrong in the try block.

This is usually too broad because it can hide unexpected problems.

Calculate the price per item by dividing the total by the quantity. Handle a failed calculation.

Make sure to pick /, followed by except.

lessons.title: The Cost of Catching Everything
lessons.interactiveContent:
Here, a bare except catches anticipated input errors, but it also catches unrelated failures.

That hides the failure type and gives every problem the same response.

lessons.title: Name the Expected Failure
lessons.interactiveContent:
A specific handler names the anticipated exception. Specific handlers keep the response connected to the operation that can fail.

We see a ValueError when a value has the correct type but is invalid for the operation.

Make sure to pick except, followed by ValueError.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A specific handler names the anticipated exception. Specific handlers keep the response connected to the operation that can fail.

We see a ValueError when a value has the correct type but is invalid for the operation.

Make sure to pick =, followed by except, and finally ValueError.

lessons.interactiveContent:

lessons.title: Put Value Error First
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also add a bare except after a specific except block. It catches other errors that the specific handler doesn't handle.

Make sure to pick except, followed by ValueError, and finally except.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can also add a bare except after a specific except block. It catches other errors that the specific handler doesn't handle.

Try to store the converted entry in quantity. Keep a separate response for invalid values and other failures.

Make sure to pick =, followed by except, ValueError, and finally except.

lessons.title: Catch Incompatible Types
lessons.interactiveContent:
Combining incompatible types, such as a number and text with +, raises TypeError.

Its handler can ask for numeric prices instead of showing a conversion response.

Make sure to pick TypeError.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Combining incompatible types, such as a number and text with +, raises TypeError.

Its handler can ask for numeric prices instead of showing a conversion response.

Make sure to pick "3", followed by TypeError.

lessons.title: When One Handler Isn't Enough
lessons.interactiveContent:
Sometimes one specific and one bare exception handler just isn't enough.

In some cases, we want to check for multiple possible specific issues.

lessons.title: One Try, Several Handlers
lessons.interactiveContent:
One try statement can have multiple except clauses.

Python checks the handlers after an exception and runs the first matching one.

Make sure to pick try followed by except and then except, except.
lessons.hardModeContent:
One try statement can have multiple except clauses.

Python checks the handlers after an exception and runs the first matching one.

Make sure to pick try, followed by /, except, except, and finally except.

lessons.title: Catch Invalid Values
lessons.interactiveContent:
The int() function raises ValueError when text like "two" can't be converted to an integer.

A matching handler can ask for a number text while leaving other failures to their own handlers.

Make sure to pick ValueError, followed by "Enter a whole number".
lessons.hardModeContent:
The int() function raises ValueError when text like "two" can't be converted to an integer.

A matching handler can ask for a number text while leaving other failures to their own handlers.

Try to store the converted number. On invalid text, print Enter a whole number.

Make sure to pick =, followed by ValueError, and finally "Enter a whole number".

Make sure to pick =, followed by "Enter a whole number", and finally "Quantity must be above zero".

lessons.title: Match Failures to Handlers - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why does it make sense to use multiple except handlers?

To handle different types of errors in different waysTo make the code run fasterTo prevent all errors from happening

To handle different types of errors in different ways.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Invalid text needs a number prompt, while a zero divisor needs a quantity prompt. How should you arrange the handlers?

Use separate ValueError and ZeroDivisionError handlers with different messages.Use one bare except handler with the number prompt for both failures.Use only ValueError because both failures involve numbers.Put both messages in the ZeroDivisionError handler.

Use separate ValueError and ZeroDivisionError handlers with different messages.
